user_direction: Preserve all accepted designs. Explore slightly larger animals and richer ecological relationships, with varied heads and coverings; creative experiments near the edges are welcome. All new animals and names remain proposals.

sheets.title: A little more weight
sheets.description: Six new animals around deer, pony and ox scale. Their added mass changes how they stand, feed and move.

takes.name: Yokejaw
takes.niche: Reed-root browser and wetland soil turner
takes.line: A deep chest and low suspended jaw let it draw tough roots out of wet ground.
takes.detail: Pony-length wetland browser, one deep NARROW torso suspended between FOUR widely set pillar-like limbs, front and rear pairs similar height, back level, short thick tail. Neck drops forward between shoulder arches; head has small high side eyes, a blunt mammalian nose pad and a deep underslung muscular LOWER JAW with a small divided gripping lip, no tusks. Jaw is only modestly wider than skull and visibly hinged, not a giant scoop. Matte dark-umber velvet on upper body gives way to bare slate neck and dull ochre overlapping scales on lower ribs. Feeding with lips on a partly exposed reed rhizome; four broad toes spread on wet ground, three-quarter left. A few disturbed reed shoots show its effect on the substrate. Preserve graceful compact strength, not a familiar horse/pig with armour.
takes.description: A deep chest and low suspended jaw let it draw tough roots out of wet ground. This proposes a reed-root browser and wetland soil turner; the relationship and detailed biology remain open.

creator_feedback.notes: LG1 generally decent; not explicitly selected among the strongest picks.

takes.name: Saltmantle
takes.line: Three pairs of slender legs carry a compact feathered trunk over soft marsh ground.
takes.detail: Red-deer-mass terrestrial wetland forager on EXACTLY SIX slender but strong legs in three staggered pairs, flat spreading three-lobed feet, compact deep chestnut-feathered trunk HIGH above ground. A small rear fan balances a SHORT downward neck at the front, no wings. Small skull with a blunt keratin upper cutting lip and fleshy lower lip, tiny lateral dark eyes, feathers join cheek continuously; head is proportionate and not an eagle pasted onto it. A short dense pale bristle brush below jaw screens mud while it picks shoots and small invertebrates. Soft creams, chestnut and slate; entire animal side-right on one marsh patch, visible six shoulder/hip connections. No decorative antlers or extra limb fans.
takes.description: Three pairs of slender legs carry a compact feathered trunk over soft marsh ground. This proposes a saltmarsh shoot and small-invertebrate forager; the relationship and detailed biology remain open.

creator_feedback.notes: LG1 generally decent. Repeated jaw frills/throat combs are disliked; do not promote that feature.

takes.name: Barrelwake
takes.line: A long swimming body channels water past two short throat combs.
takes.detail: Ox-length but streamlined aquatic animal with one LONG low horizontal trunk, FOUR broad steering FLIPPERS in two paired girdles and a short horizontal tail blade. Slate-green matte skin with small dull bronze scales on back. Skull broad and low, fish-informed small side eyes and tight nostrils; two short flexible filter combs lie along the throat corners and open subtly into water, rooted in continuous gill/jaw tissue. Normal modest mouth and lean body; no huge gape, fat bulbous belly or teeth. Facing left in shallow clear water, FULL body, four flippers and tail visible; tiny cloudy stream entering throat and cleaner water behind are implied without diagram arrows. No lizard head or whale face copied.
takes.description: A long swimming body channels water past two short throat combs. This proposes a shallow-channel suspension feeder; the relationship and detailed biology remain open.

creator_feedback.notes: Repeated filter-feeder-looking jaw frills / throat combs are overused and disliked. Whole animal not explicitly rejected.

takes.name: Vaultstalker
takes.line: A high shoulder arch shelters the head while low rear limbs brace a sudden forward push.
takes.detail: Large-deer-mass four-legged predator with a narrow high arched SHOULDER ring, LONG strong forelimbs and much SHORTER thick hindlimbs beneath a low pelvis; back slopes DOWN to the rear. Long broad counterbalancing tail kept low. Coarse silver-brown fur grows in broken shoulder mats, fine matte scales protect long front shins; neck is short and draws back beneath arch. Small mammalian skull has a narrow flexible nose, low rounded ears, modest forward-looking eyes and tight closed lips over a deep bite, no large fangs or cat/dog mask. Full three-quarter right, crouched on broken stone with all four limbs readable, alert rather than roaring. Body built as its own animal, not a hulking gorilla.
takes.description: A high shoulder arch shelters the head while low rear limbs brace a sudden forward push. This proposes a broken-ground ambush predator; the relationship and detailed biology remain open.

creator_feedback.notes: Liked a lot: like a larger honey badger with scales. Preserve the original face, body, high shoulders, coat and scaled forelimbs.

takes.name: Pithbreaker
takes.size: A little larger than a small armadillo · exact size open
takes.line: Two braced forefeet open rotten wood while a narrow mouth reaches the exposed galleries.
takes.detail: Black-bear-mass terrestrial insect specialist, FOUR limbs: two heavily muscled long forearms with a single broad blunt digging claw among shorter toes, two shorter broad hindfeet. Compact wedge trunk narrows rearward, short flattened tail. Dull deep-blue keratin plates form flexible longitudinal bands along back, cinnamon short fur on underside. Low neckless mammalian head with small nose pad, deeply inset eyes, minute protected ears, SMALL narrow toothless mouth and one short fine tongue reaching an opened rotten log. Skull, jaw and shoulders form one stout load-bearing unit; no giant anteater snout or pasted armadillo face. Side-left, log opened by hands and a few tiny insect marks, body and feet fully visible.
takes.description: Two braced forefeet open rotten wood while a narrow mouth reaches the exposed galleries. This proposes a colonial-insect specialist; the relationship and detailed biology remain open.

creator_feedback.notes: Liked. Make it visibly a little larger than a small armadillo; scale should be clear. Exact dimensions remain open.

takes.name: Mantlebrood
takes.size: Small-pony mass · about 1.1 m at shoulder
takes.line: Two shallow flank folds shelter its young while the adult continues browsing.
takes.detail: Small-pony-sized long slim quadrupedal browser on FOUR moderate-length muscular legs, horizontal ribcage, rounded low pelvis, short upright neck and long soft blunt mammalian muzzle with narrow split lip, modest side eyes and tiny ear cuffs. Matte warm grey skin under short cocoa fur; TWO shallow flexible skin-and-fur brood pockets fold along LOWER FLANKS, anatomically continuous with belly, not a basket or armour. One small juvenile with matching face and limbs peeks out of a single pocket; other pocket closed. Juvenile reads as offspring, not an extra adult head or limb. Adult has one head, four legs and short tail. Full side-right beside shrub, restrained and appealing living anatomy, no exposed organs.
takes.description: Two shallow flank folds shelter its young while the adult continues browsing. This proposes a brooding browser; the relationship and detailed biology remain open.

creator_feedback.notes: Liked; familiar kangaroo-like corollary with distinct unusual anatomy. Preserve the corrected small furred brood pocket and original animal.

generation_history.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit only the LOWER-RIGHT sixth animal in the attached six-creature Breachline study sheet. Preserve the other FIVE animals, their positions, sizes, painted materials, habitat fragments, background, lighting and brushwork exactly. Preserve the sixth adult's existing slim quadruped body, four legs, head, neck, face, short tail and coat. Correct only its brood anatomy: replace the large hanging bare udder-like sac and protruding nipples with TWO SMALL, shallow, matte, cocoa-furred lateral brood folds integrated closely into the LOWER FLANK, one visible, the far side mostly concealed. These are narrow horizontal protective slits tucked just behind the ribcage, NOT low pendulous belly bags. The adult belly must remain slim and fur-covered. Exactly ONE very small matching juvenile's head and forepaws peek from the visible narrow slit. Juvenile head is no larger than the adult's eye-to-nose length. No nipples, no exposed udder, no large bare skin patches, no added adult heads or limbs. Keep this a clear restrained experiment in lateral brood care and maintain plausible anatomy. Landscape 1536x1024, no typography, no other changes.

sheets.title: Stranger lives
sheets.description: Six bolder proposals let relationships and life history shape the animal. These deliberately test the edges of the direction.

takes.name: Pollenferry
takes.size: Fallow-deer mass · body about 1.4 m long
takes.niche: Ground-level nectar feeder and pollen carrier
takes.line: A low feeding front and a protected throat brush let it reach deep flowers without crushing them.
takes.detail: Fallow-deer-mass land animal with a slim flattened torso, FOUR short backward-folding muscular legs and broad padded feet straddling low flowers. No wings. A long narrow flexible neck extends below chest and ends in a small mammalian skull with closable slit nostrils, modest lateral eyes and a short tubular upper lip, no giant nose or beak. A compact tawny bristle pad under chin and throat collects pale pollen; short soft ochre fur elsewhere grades into pebbled teal skin on bare limbs. One broad low flower meets the mouth so throat brush visibly touches anthers; flowers are separate plants, not growing from animal. Tail short and heavy. Whole side-left on tiny patch; head-neck-feeding tube are continuous restrained anatomy, not a flower creature.
takes.description: A low feeding front and a protected throat brush let it reach deep flowers without crushing them. This proposes a ground-level nectar feeder and pollen carrier; the relationship and detailed biology remain open.

creator_feedback.notes: Thicker leathery skin transitioning into feather/fur looks cool. Preserve that material relationship. Avoid recurring exaggerated jaw/throat combs.

takes.name: Drylock
takes.niche: Seasonal floodplain hunter with dry-season dormancy
takes.line: Its flexible skin seals moisture around the body when the seasonal pools disappear.
takes.detail: Large-dog-mass amphibious animal, streamlined elongated ribcage on FOUR short paddle-footed limbs, long tapering tail. Matte blue-grey naked skin carries thick ochre protective ridges along sides that can meet under belly; this is one living skin covering, not shell halves. Small elongated AMPHIBIAN skull, modest raised lateral eyes, narrow closed mouth and simple nostrils, no smile. Main animal awake stepping out of a broken mud cocoon at a newly wetted pool edge; thin empty dry crust lies behind it to suggest dormancy, not a second animal, exuvia or gore. Feet and full tail visible, side-right. Skin has subtle folds needed for sealing but avoid inflated balloon body.
takes.description: Its flexible skin seals moisture around the body when the seasonal pools disappear. This proposes a seasonal floodplain hunter with dry-season dormancy; the relationship and detailed biology remain open.

takes.name: Tidemason
takes.niche: Sessile shore filter feeder and habitat builder
takes.line: A fixed adult grows a low shell ridge that retains a small pool at low tide.
takes.detail: A BOAR-LENGTH SESSILE marine animal on a low shoreline rock, an ORIGINAL coherent mollusc-like body: broad muscular attached foot, one tough low asymmetrical ridge of chalk-and-ochre shell, and a single pale mantle with TWO short muscular water siphons. No face, eyes, legs, wings, plants or human mouth. Filter-feeding siphons visibly arise from same soft mantle beneath shell rim. Its low shell diverts a tiny wave and encloses one small tide pool containing two tiny shrimp-like residents; no city, coral tree or huge walking reef. The animal looks tactile, weighty and alive, not architecture. FULL shell and foot visible in three-quarter left, shallow-water vignette, broad ivory and mineral-green paint.
takes.description: A fixed adult grows a low shell ridge that retains a small pool at low tide. This proposes a sessile shore filter feeder and habitat builder; the detailed biology remains open.

takes.name: Barkdrummer
takes.line: A short striking nose opens bark seams before a fine tongue reaches the prey beneath.
takes.detail: Deer-mass four-legged tree-edge insect hunter with short compact rear trunk and TWO LONG powerful forelimbs braced against a slanted fallen trunk, two short hindlimbs firmly grounded, broad balancing tail resting behind. Dense charcoal FEATHERS on body, dull copper scutes on front wrists. Head small and deeply integrated into a reinforced short neck: flattened blunt KERATIN nasal striking pad above a narrow probing mouth, small rear-set eyes, no external ears and no large bird beak. Shows head pulled a little back from a bark seam, not dramatic hammer motion. A short fine tongue at lip and opened bark imply feeding. Full body and supports visible, three-quarter right; no tool held, no equipment.
takes.description: A short striking nose opens bark seams before a fine tongue reaches the prey beneath. This proposes a wood-boring prey specialist; the relationship and detailed biology remain open.

creator_feedback.notes: Liked head plate and feather-scale combination. Creator notes overlap with number 5; likely Pithbreaker, but exact comparison not explicitly specified. Do not merge their identities.

takes.name: Sporewarden
takes.line: A sheltered flank patch feeds a modest fungal growth that the animal tends and grazes.
takes.detail: Sheep-to-deer-mass animal with a VERY narrow deep torso on SIX short sturdy legs in three pairs, long low neck and small soft MAMMALIAN browsing muzzle with divided lip, matte nose and modest side eyes, tiny folded ears. Short rust fur on upper body, smooth dark belly. One shallow porous skin patch on EACH flank sustains low compact pale edible fungus nodules, only a hand-span patch, not tall mushrooms or foliage. The animal bends its own neck to nip one nodule from its near flank; jaw, neck and back remain connected and readable. Mutualism is subtle surface biology on an ordinary coherent living animal, no walking garden or monster. Whole side-left on woodland litter, muted russet and cream.
takes.description: A sheltered flank patch feeds a modest fungal growth that the animal tends and grazes. This proposes a fungal-garden grazer and spore disperser; the relationship and detailed biology remain open.

creator_feedback.notes: A little gross, but the animal is liked. Test it without fungus. Original fungal symbiosis is not accepted; revised animal needs review.

takes.name: Scalelease
takes.size: Large-dog mass · body about 1.4 m long
takes.line: Small tenants shelter beneath broad back scales; the host gains their grooming activity.
takes.detail: Large-dog-mass long LOW quadrupedal herbivore, exactly FOUR strong legs with blunt split toes, short neck, broad low skull with SMALL REPTILIAN cheek scales and a restrained broad grinding lower lip, modest narrow eyes. Entire body covered in dull teal overlapping scales, with four broad back scutes slightly lifted at edges to make natural shallow dry pockets while still attached to skin. Exactly TWO tiny brown many-legged grooming animals sit beneath separate raised scute rims, scaled clearly as small tenants, not extra host limbs or ornamental parasites. One grazes debris at scale root. Host has one ordinary broad tapering tail, lean body, no glowing magic. Whole three-quarter right on damp rock; only one adult host.
takes.description: Small tenants shelter beneath broad back scales; the host gains their grooming activity. This proposes a shelter-sharing grazer; the relationship and detailed biology remain open.

creator_feedback.notes: Bugs underneath the scales do not make sense to the creator. Exclude this design from future references; preserve shared source sheet for the liked cells.
